schema.title: C4OS Grill Question 041 - Config TOML And Tool Policy

questions.label: How should C4OS treat config.toml?
questions.help: Recommended: both user-editable and UI-editable, with Settings preserving unknown keys/comments where possible and surfacing parse errors clearly.
options: Generated file; users should not edit directly

questions.label: What scope should per-tool policy defaults use?
questions.help: Recommended: user-global defaults with session-level narrowing. This matches user-owned app settings while preventing a session from silently widening authority.
options: Layered user, workspace, project, and session policy

questions.label: Which settings belong in config.toml first?
questions.help: Recommended: keep config.toml useful for runtime, provider/model defaults, plugin marketplace sources, plugin enablement, and app-tool policy. Secrets stay in secure storage.
options: Runtime, provider/model defaults, marketplaces, plugin enablement, and app-tool policy

questions.label: When Settings UI and config.toml disagree, which wins?
questions.help: Recommended: config.toml is the persisted source; Settings edits write to it. Parse errors keep last valid config and show a blocking Settings error.
options: config.toml is source; Settings writes to it; parse errors keep last valid config
Settings database wins and rewrites config.toml
Ask the user on every conflict
